Learning

Evidence and decisions

Quick readMore contextTechnical detailSpeaker notes

How can a partnership show why it made a decision, and revise it when evidence changes?

My example

When AI helps with research, someone later has to ask: what evidence supports this claim, what is still uncertain, and what was this action allowed to do? GKOS is my developing approach to keeping those links.

Provenance lets people inspect a claim. It does not make the claim true.

in development

A practical next step

Test one evidence record that connects a claim, its sources, review, limits, and next decision.

Progress would mean: A new reviewer can trace the claim to evidence and explain what changed after review.

Who needs to be involved

Researchers, evidence reviewers, tool builders, and the people using the result.

Research stage: Across the research journey.

More context

  • AI-assisted work needs records of sources, transformations, checks, authorization, and resulting actions.
  • Reviewers should be able to see what supports a claim, what remains uncertain, and what an action was authorized to do.
  • Corrections stay visible as new versions instead of silently rewriting history.

Evidence and technical detail

RepositoryRoleStatus
gkos-standardPre-standard for evidence lineage, authority, dispositions, governance responsibilities, conformance fixturesdocumented
GKOS-EngineTypeScript reference engine: parsing, validation, lineage, knowledge graph, retrieval, citationsdocumented
GKOS-Engine-RustGround-up Rust implementation; implementation and qualification records; consult the current repository for statusin development
GKOS-Engine-LiteRust retrieval and restricted-profile work; conformance and adversarial casesin development
model-capability-manifest-standardDeclare AI capability through structured, testable, versioned evidence rather than model namesproposed

Proposed division of labor: AI extracts metadata and proposes classifications and related records; deterministic checks enforce allowed values, required evidence, and consistency; humans review ambiguity and consequential interpretation. Deterministic rules can enforce record integrity. They cannot make scientific interpretation automatically correct, so conflicting interpretations stay attributable and inspectable.
